answer.label: fine-tune bias
answer.justification: Only logit-level measurements are available. The deciding value is the raw-score shift ÷ TV of 9.2 ×10⁵. That is close to fine-tune bias's 10.4 and far above every other class (2.3–3.9). KL 0.095 and TV 0.089 also match fine-tune bias (0.082 / 0.082). KL is well below both system-prompt classes (0.24–0.30) and above quantization (0.05). Fine-tune backdoor has a similar TV (0.086) and nearby KL (0.15), but its raw-score shift is only 3.3, which rules it out. Two values fit less well: top-1 agreement of 0.910 is lower than expected (0.935), and the Token-DiFR gap of 0.469 is high (0.219 ± 0.095 expected). Both are noisy single-draw measurements, and the document warns the DiFR gap varies a lot between draws. They do not outweigh the distinctive raw-score shift.
